Gmail best practices:
- To open an email, click directly on the email subject/preview text, NOT the checkbox or star
- Use keyboard shortcuts: 'c' to compose, 'r' to reply, 'a' to reply all, 'f' to forward, 'e' to archive
- To search, use the search bar at the top with operators like 'from:', 'to:', 'subject:', 'is:unread'
- Reading pane may be on the right or below depending on user settings - check which layout is active
- Verification codes are often in emails from 'noreply@' addresses with subjects containing 'verification', 'code', or 'confirm'

Google Docs best practices:
- This is a canvas-based application - use screenshots to see content, read_page may not capture all text
- Use keyboard shortcuts: Cmd/Ctrl+B for bold, Cmd/Ctrl+I for italic, Cmd/Ctrl+K for links
- To navigate, use Cmd/Ctrl+F to find text, then click on the result
- For editing, click to place cursor then type - triple-click to select a paragraph
- Access menus via the menu bar at the top (File, Edit, View, Insert, Format, etc.)

Google Sheets best practices:
- Click on cells to select them, double-click to edit cell content
- Use Tab to move right, Enter to move down, arrow keys to navigate
- Formulas start with '=' - e.g., =SUM(A1:A10), =VLOOKUP(), =IF()
- Use Cmd/Ctrl+C and Cmd/Ctrl+V for copy/paste
- Select ranges by clicking and dragging, or Shift+click for range selection

GitHub best practices:
- Repository navigation: Code tab for files, Issues for bug tracking, Pull requests for code review
- To view a file, click on the filename in the file tree
- Use 't' to open file finder, 'l' to jump to a line
- In PRs: 'Files changed' tab shows diffs, 'Conversation' tab shows comments
- Use the search bar with qualifiers: 'is:open is:pr', 'is:issue label:bug'

SimplifyJobs / job-aggregator GitHub repos — verified patterns

Applies ONLY when the current URL path matches one of these aggregator repos:
- /SimplifyJobs/New-Grad-Positions
- /SimplifyJobs/Summer{YEAR}-Internships
- /ouckah/Summer{YEAR}-Internships
- /vanshb03/Summer{YEAR}-Internships
- any README that renders a markdown table of open jobs with an 'Apply' column
If the URL is a normal GitHub repo (code/issues/PRs), ignore this skill and use the general GitHub skill above.

## What this page is
- A community-maintained README rendered as a markdown table of currently-open jobs
- Columns: Company | Role | Location | Apply | Age (date posted)
- The 'Apply' cell is an <a> link that leaves GitHub and lands on the company's ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, iCIMS, Ashby, SmartRecruiters, etc.)
- This is NOT a job board with its own application flow — GitHub is only the directory

## Picking the right job
- read_page returns the table rows with each Apply link having its own ref number — click by ref, NEVER by screen coordinates (coordinates shift with viewport width and you'll hit the wrong row)
- Multiple rows per company are normal (different roles/locations) — confirm role and location before clicking Apply
- 🔒 emoji on a row means the role is closed — skip it; the link will 404 or show 'no longer accepting'
- The repo has multiple anchor sections (Software Engineering, Quant Finance, Product Management, Hardware, etc.) — the URL fragment (e.g. #-software-engineering-new-grad-roles) tells you which section the user opened. Stay in that section unless the user asks otherwise
- Newest jobs are at the top of each section

## After clicking Apply
- The link may open in the SAME tab (replacing the GitHub page) or a NEW tab — call tabs_context immediately after the click to confirm before doing anything else
- If a new tab opened, switch to it. Do NOT click Apply again on the GitHub tab — repeating clicks creates duplicate ATS tabs (seen multiple times in past runs)
- Once on the ATS, use the matching domain skill (greenhouse.io, lever.co, myworkdayjobs.com, ashbyhq.com, icims.com, smartrecruiters.com, tesla.com) for that flow

## Third-party extension overlays (CRITICAL — ignore these)
- Other Chrome extensions (e.g. 'jobright-helper-plugin', 'simplify-helper') inject sidebars and modals onto SimplifyJobs pages
- These overlays are NOT part of GitHub or part of the user's task — they have their own buttons ('AUTO FILL', 'CONTINUE', 'NEED HELP?', etc.) that belong to a different product
- Do NOT click any overlay button. Do NOT treat overlay content as page content. If read_page surfaces an element from a shadow root with id 'jobright-helper-plugin' or a class starting with 'jobright-' / 'simplify-', skip it
- The user's apply flow only uses the markdown table — ignore everything else

## Token efficiency
- The README is long (50K+ characters). Use read_page with the default max_chars; do NOT request 80000 or higher — the visible viewport rarely needs more than 25K of DOM
- Scroll first to put the row you want in the viewport, THEN read_page once and click — avoid scanning the whole page in one read

Reddit UI patterns:
- Posts are listed in a feed - click on post title to view full post and comments
- Comments are nested/threaded - each comment has its own reply button underneath
- Upvote (up arrow) and downvote (down arrow) buttons are to the left of each post/comment
- To comment, scroll to comment box at top of comments section, or click reply under a specific comment
- Use the search bar at top to find subreddits or posts
- r/subredditname format for community names

JobRight job aggregator — verified patterns

## What this is
- JobRight lists recommended jobs as cards at jobright.ai/jobs/recommend. Each card has an 'Apply with Autofill' button and the job title links to a detail page (jobright.ai/jobs/info/{id}).
- 'Apply with Autofill' is JobRight's OWN feature — it opens the real employer ATS (Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, iCIMS, Ashby, Tesla, etc.) in a NEW TAB.

## Applying (CRITICAL — avoid the click loop)
1. Click 'Apply with Autofill' (or the job title → then Apply) ONCE.
2. Immediately call tabs_context. The ATS almost always opens in a NEW TAB (openedByAgent:false). Switch to that new tab and proceed there.
3. If after ONE click + a 2s wait + tabs_context NO new tab appeared and the JobRight URL did not change: do NOT click 'Apply with Autofill' again — repeated clicks do nothing and burn turns (this caused a 20-turn dead loop in a past run). Instead, click the job TITLE to open the detail page, then click the Apply button there.
4. Never click the same Apply button more than twice. If two clicks produce no new tab and no navigation, move to the next job card or report that JobRight's autofill did not launch.

## 'Did you apply?' modal
- After you finish on the ATS and return to the JobRight tab, JobRight may show a 'Did you apply?' / confirmation modal. This is a real blocking dialog — read it (take a screenshot if read_page doesn't show it) and click 'Yes, I applied' (or equivalent) to dismiss before continuing to the next job.

## Enable Autofill prompt
- The first time, JobRight may show an 'Enable Autofill' dialog. Click 'Yes, Enable Autofill Now' once. If it navigates to /jobs/profile, navigate back to /jobs/recommend and resume.

## Token efficiency
- The recommend page DOM is large. Use read_page with default max_chars; do NOT request 60000-80000 — it inflates cost (one past run spent $0.03+ per 80K read) without revealing more cards. Scroll to bring a card into view, then read once and click its ref.

iCIMS ATS — verified patterns

## Application Flow
- 'Apply' / 'Apply Now' on the job page → a login/email step ('Enter Your Information') → Candidate Profile → Candidate Questions → EEO → Submit.
- The email step: fill the email field, click Next. iCIMS emails a verification but usually proceeds straight to the candidate profile.

## Resume upload (CRITICAL)
- The resume file input is inside a SHADOW DOM. Use the file_upload tool with the numeric ref from read_page — it resolves backendNodeIds and pierces shadow DOM. Do NOT fall back to clicking 'My Computer' and typing into the OS dialog (the agent cannot see OS dialogs).
- After uploading, iCIMS may STILL show 'Please upload your resume: required' for a moment, or may have actually accepted it. Call read_page and look for a hidden input like PortalProfileFields.Resume_FileName with your filename as its value — if present, the resume IS uploaded; proceed to Submit. Do not re-upload in a loop.

## Dropdowns
- iCIMS uses native-like <select> dropdowns — use form_input. They do NOT have a LinkedIn option for 'How did you hear about us?'. Available options are typically: Company Website, Email Campaign, Job Board, Job Fair, Other, Referred by a current employee, Social Media. Pick 'Job Board' (closest to LinkedIn/aggregator referral).
- Race/ethnicity options use full labels e.g. 'Asian (Not Hispanic or Latino)', not just 'Asian'. Pass the full label.

## Known edge cases
- iCIMS often embeds content in an iframe (#icims_content_iframe) — element refs from read_page still work via file_upload/form_input.
- After clicking Submit on the final step the URL changes to .../job?mode=submit_apply and shows 'Your application was submitted successfully.' — that is the only success confirmation; stop there.

## Token efficiency
- read_page with default max_chars is enough; the form is compact once you are on the candidate page.

LinkedIn Job Application — verified patterns

## Easy Apply Flow
- Click 'Easy Apply' button on the job listing to open the modal
- The modal is a multi-step form — each step has a 'Next' or 'Review' button at the bottom
- Contact Info page is pre-filled from LinkedIn profile — do NOT modify, just click Next
- Modal forms may need scrolling to see all content and buttons — scroll inside the modal
- Use screenshots over read_page for modals — accessibility tree often misses modal content
- After the final step, there is a 'Submit application' button — this is the only place to pause
- Some steps ask additional questions (years of experience, work authorization, etc.)
- For dropdowns in the modal, ALWAYS use form_input — custom React dropdowns break with clicks
- Resume upload: if prompted, use file_upload tool — never click the upload button directly

## External Apply
- 'Apply' (without 'Easy') redirects to the company's ATS (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, etc.)
- A new tab may open — use tabs_context to find it, then continue in that tab

## Navigation
- Main tabs: Home (feed), My Network, Jobs, Messaging, Notifications
- Job search: Jobs tab, then filter by location, experience level, date posted
- 'Easy Apply' = apply within LinkedIn modal; 'Apply' = external site

## Known Issues
- Modal can be dismissed by clicking outside — be careful with coordinate clicks
- 'Additional Questions' step may have required fields — fill all before clicking Next
- Phone number field may have a country code dropdown — use form_input for both parts
- If a 'Follow' checkbox appears, leave it as-is

Indeed Job Application — verified patterns

## Applying
- Click 'Apply now' on the job listing page (right panel or top of description)
- Indeed has its own application flow — multi-step form
- Resume may be pre-attached from Indeed profile — check and skip if already there
- Contact info is usually pre-filled — verify and click Continue
- Additional questions vary by employer — fill all required fields
- Final step has 'Submit your application' button

## Navigation
- Search: 'What' (job title/keywords) and 'Where' (location) fields at top
- Filter: date posted, salary estimate, job type, experience level on left sidebar
- Click job title to view description; apply button is typically on right panel
- Some jobs redirect to external company sites

## Edge Cases
- 'Apply on company site' opens the employer's ATS in a new tab
- Indeed may ask screening questions before showing the full application
- Assessments may be required — these are timed tests, escalate if encountered

## Token efficiency
- Use get_page_text to read job descriptions; use read_page only for form interaction
- On form pages, read_page with max_chars=20000 is sufficient; only increase if fields appear cut off

Workday ATS — verified patterns

## Application Flow
- Click 'Apply' button on the job page to start
- Workday uses a multi-step wizard: My Information → My Experience → Application Questions → Voluntary Disclosures → Self-Identify → Review → Submit
- 'Autofill with Resume' or 'Apply with LinkedIn' buttons may appear at the top — use them if available to pre-fill fields
- Each section has a 'Save and Continue' or 'Next' button at the bottom

## Form Patterns (CRITICAL)
- Workday uses custom React/web components — ALWAYS use form_input for plain text/dropdown selects

### Typeahead 'prompt' fields (Field of Study, School, Skills, Location, Source) — READ THIS, it is the #1 cause of stuck runs
- These are SEARCH boxes, not selects. form_input only TYPES the query into them — it does NOT commit a choice. Pressing Enter does nothing. Clicking by screen coordinate misses. A real run burned 25+ turns and $0.73 because the agent kept doing exactly those three things.
- Correct procedure, every time:
  1. form_input the field with a SHORT query — one keyword, e.g. 'Engineer' or 'Computer', NOT a full phrase like 'Engineering Science'. Short queries return more options.
  2. read_page. The open results now appear at the TOP of the output under '=== OPEN DROPDOWN / OPTION LIST ===', each option with its own [ref].
  3. computer left_click the matching option BY ITS [ref]. That click is what commits the selection.
  4. read_page once more to confirm the field now shows the chosen value.
- If NO exact match exists, pick the closest available option and click its ref — do NOT keep re-typing the same field hoping for a better match. Total budget per prompt field: type → read → click → confirm (≈4 turns). If it is still empty after that, move on; do not loop.
- NEVER use javascript_tool to set the field value or .value — Workday ignores it and the selection won't persist.
- Date fields: click the field, a calendar or date picker appears — type the date directly in MM/DD/YYYY format
- For 'How Did You Hear About Us': use form_input with the source text
- Required fields marked with asterisk (*) — fill ALL before proceeding
- Radio buttons: use computer left_click with the element ref

## CC-305 Disability Form
- This is a US federal form — appears in Voluntary Self-Identification section
- Has Name field, Date field (signature date), and disability status radio buttons
- For the date: open the calendar picker and click today's date (highlighted), OR type today's date
- Select the appropriate disability option radio button

## EEO / Diversity Section
- Gender, Race/Ethnicity, Veteran Status dropdowns
- These are OPTIONAL in many implementations but may be required
- Use form_input for each dropdown

## Known Edge Cases
- Workday pages load slowly — wait 3-5 seconds after navigation before reading
- 'Sign In' may be required — check if already signed in via SSO
- Some Workday instances use *.myworkdayjobs.com, others use *.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com or *.wd5.myworkdayjobs.com
- File upload for resume: use file_upload tool, never click the upload button
- 'Already Applied' message may appear — if so, the job was already applied to, stop and report

## Token efficiency
- Use get_page_text to read job descriptions; use read_page only for form interaction
- On Workday form pages, read_page with max_chars=20000 captures all fields; only increase if a section appears cut off

Greenhouse ATS — verified patterns

## Application Flow
- Job page has an 'Apply for this job' button — click it
- Single long form (not multi-step): all fields on one page
- Sections: Personal Information, Resume/Cover Letter, Custom Questions, EEO (optional)
- 'Submit Application' button at the bottom

## Form Patterns
- Standard HTML form inputs — form_input works well for all fields
- Resume upload: file input element — use file_upload tool
- Cover letter: may be a textarea or file upload
- Custom questions vary by company — fill all required fields
- LinkedIn/GitHub/Portfolio URL fields are common
- Dropdowns are usually native <select> elements — form_input handles them

## Known Edge Cases
- Some companies embed Greenhouse in an iframe on their own domain
- The form may be long — scroll down to find all sections
- 'Are you legally authorized to work in the United States?' is common
- 'Will you now or in the future require sponsorship?' is common

## Token efficiency
- Use get_page_text to read job descriptions; use read_page only for form interaction
- Greenhouse forms are compact — read_page with max_chars=20000 is sufficient

Tesla Careers — verified patterns

## Application Flow
- Tesla's careers SPA is at tesla.com/careers — it is NOT redirected to an external ATS
- The form has 3 steps: Personal Info → Experience/Documents → Legal Acknowledgment
- Each step has a 'Next' button at the bottom; the final step has 'Submit'
- After clicking Next, call read_page and wait for the next step to fully load before proceeding

## Phone Number Field (CRITICAL)
- The phone field has TWO separate elements: a TDS country code button and a plain text input
- The country code button defaults to 'US +1' — if the applicant is US-based, DO NOT touch this button
- Only fill the phone number text input (the plain input field next to the dropdown button)
- Attempting to re-select 'US +1' on an already-correct dropdown wastes retries and may fail

## TDS Custom Dropdowns
- Tesla Design System (TDS) dropdowns use aria-haspopup='listbox' with role='option' items
- There is NO search input inside TDS listboxes — form_input clicks the trigger and matches option by textContent
- Options use full text (e.g., 'United States', 'California') — pass full names to form_input
- If form_input fails: use Step C fallback — computer left_click on the trigger, read_page to see options with refs, computer left_click on the matching option ref

## Multi-Step Navigation
- Click 'Next' only after all required fields on the current step are filled and verified (4d check)
- If validation errors appear after clicking Next, stay on the same step and fix the flagged fields
- Do not click 'Submit' until the final (Step 3) Legal Acknowledgment page

## Legal Acknowledgment (Step 3)
- Contains a legal agreement with a required checkbox — check it before submitting
- Links to Tesla Talent Privacy Notice and Arbitration Agreement are informational — do not click them
- E-Verify notice is informational — no interaction needed

## Tesla Account
- If a login/signup page appears before or during the application, use Account Credentials from the Applicant Profile
- After login, navigate back to the job listing URL and click Apply again to resume

X/Twitter — verified patterns (updated 2026-03-30)

## Reading pages (CRITICAL)
- X loads content asynchronously — page looks empty for 3-5 seconds after navigation.
- read_page often returns ONLY "To view keyboard shortcuts" — tweets haven't loaded yet.
- DO NOT re-navigate to the same URL. That resets loading and makes it worse.
- Instead: wait 5 seconds, then use get_page_text — it reads visible text and is more reliable.
- If get_page_text returns nothing, scroll down once and try again.

## Search
- URL: x.com/search?q={encoded_query}&src=typed_query&f=live
- After navigating, wait 5 seconds, then get_page_text (NOT read_page).
- Scroll down once to load more tweets, then get_page_text again.
- Tweet URLs in page text follow pattern: /status/{id}

## Text input (CRITICAL — Draft.js)
- form_input DOES NOT WORK — Draft.js ignores programmatic input.
- computer type action GARBLES TEXT.
- ONLY RELIABLE METHOD — use javascript_tool:
  document.querySelector('[data-testid="tweetTextarea_0"]').focus();
  document.execCommand('insertText', false, 'your reply text here');
- Always verify text appeared by reading after insertion.

## Replying to a tweet
1. Navigate to tweet URL (x.com/{handle}/status/{id})
2. Wait 3 seconds, read the page
3. Click the reply/comment icon (speech bubble) in the action bar
4. Use javascript_tool to insert text (see above)
5. Verify text appeared, then click blue "Reply" button
6. Wait 2 seconds to confirm reply posted

## Known traps
- DO NOT scroll looking for "Post your reply" — reply box appears after clicking comment icon
- x.com/compose/post may open — that's fine, type and click Reply there
- "Leave site?" dialog — ALWAYS click Cancel, finish posting first
- Reply button is disabled until text is entered — verify first
- Space replies 15+ seconds apart (rate limiting)
- NEVER navigate to the same URL you're already on
